title: People's Republic of Zanzibar
capsule: The People's Republic of Zanzibar existed for 99 days, from 12 January 1964 — when the Zanzibar Revolution overthrew Sultan Jamshid bin Abdullah and killed or expelled most of the Arab and South Asian elite — to 26 April 1964, when President Abeid Karume signed the Act of Union with mainland Tanganyika to create the United Republic of Tanzania. The revolution was led by the Afro-Shirazi Party and the Umma Party under John Okello and then Karume; it was one of the bloodiest post-colonial upheavals in East Africa, with estimates of between 5,000 and 20,000 killed. The union preserved Zanzibar's internal autonomy as a semi-autonomous region under its own Revolutionary Council.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The geographic extent — the islands of Unguja and Pemba — is precisely known; casualty figures for the revolution remain contested in the scholarly literature.
